rounds_summary.round_1: Original study: 2 skills x 2 arms x 3 models = 6 cells. 3 of 6 cells sign-flipped negative. Aggregate +2.5%.
rounds_summary.round_2: Post-fix re-run of skills-freshness only after PR #18 tightened its SKILL.md. 3 of 3 cells positive. Aggregate +11%. All sign-flipped cells turned around.
rounds_summary.round_3: Rigor-exempt label test on content-audit (Spacepotatis project skill). Result: not deep-negative as assumed; sat at break-even (+1%). Label inflated.
rounds_summary.round_4: Post-fix re-run of content-audit after a cap was added to step 2. Result: MIXED. 1 of 2 negative cells flipped (haiku +16pp), aggregate moved from +1% to +4%, but sonnet regressed -6pp.
rounds_summary.round_5: Re-validation of both new skills (skills-freshness, skills-quality) at current state. Result: MIXED per goal. Aggregate strongly positive (+16% across 6 cells) but one cell (opus skills-quality) showed -62% — an N=1 anomaly from an anomalously cheap cold-walk.

round_3.context: Test whether rigor-exempt label was real or assumed
round_3.finding: Content-audit sits at break-even, not deep-negative as the rigor-exempt label assumed. The label was inflated. Wholesale exemption from cost-trap rules would silence a genuine signal.

round_4.fix: Added 'at most 5 traces, batch into a single grep with alternation if more, don't spelunk per-id' cap to step 2 of content-audit/SKILL.md

goal_stated_up_front.MIXED: 1 cell flips AND aggregate moves but <+5%

round_4.verdict: MIXED — 1 of 2 negative cells flipped (haiku), aggregate moved +3pp from +1% to +4% but stayed under +5%. The cost-trap rule's prediction is correct on smaller models; the fix may slightly hurt larger models that don't over-execute.

round_5.context: Re-validate Round 1 + Round 2 results — test repeatability vs N=1 noise

aggregate_6_cells.note: 6 cells (2 skills x 3 models), 12 agents (BEFORE+AFTER per cell); ratio-of-sums

goal_stated_up_front.PASS: skills-freshness >=2 cells positive AND skills-quality direction matches Round 1 AND aggregate > 0

round_5.verdict: MIXED — skills-freshness passed (2 of 3 cells positive, Round 2 was 3 of 3); skills-quality did not directionally match Round 1 (1 of 3 cells match sign); but aggregate is strongly positive at +16% (best of any round)

anomalies.opus_quality_minus_62: Cell BEFORE was 31K tokens — anomalously cheap, suggests opus short-circuited the cold-walk without thoroughly auditing. AFTER (51K) was more representative. The -62% delta is an artifact of an unusually cheap cold-walk baseline, not a sign of the optimization hurting opus on this skill.
anomalies.haiku_quality_plus_54: Haiku continues to be the most consistent beneficiary of the optimization across all rounds — same investigation-collapse pattern.

stable_findings_across_rounds: Haiku consistently benefits most from bounded SKILL.md guidance (Round 1 +17% to +54%, Round 2 +20%, Round 4 +16pp flip, Round 5 +48% / +54%)
Aggregate save trends positive — small in Round 1 (+2.5%), strong in Round 5 (+16%) — the optimization principle holds in the aggregate even when individual cells show high N=1 variance
Opus is the most variable model, with single-cell swings up to 67pp between rounds (skills-quality/opus +5% R1 to -62% R5) — measurement noise dominates for this model at N=1
cross_round_synthesis.what_the_5_rounds_collectively_show: The 'maximize local computation, minimize LLM tokens' principle is real and the cost-trap rules in skills-quality detect genuine waste. The fix's effectiveness is model-dependent: smaller models (Haiku) benefit reliably, larger models (Opus) show variable response. N=1 per cell is sufficient to surface direction but not magnitude — the headline numbers should always be read with that caveat. Wholesale rigor-exempt labels are inflated; per-finding judgment is the right level of skepticism.
